planted.class: Debug mode left on in production
planted.note: env('APP_DEBUG', true) defaults to true, so any host that does not explicitly set APP_DEBUG serves Laravel's Whoops page with stack frames, environment variables and database credentials to unauthenticated visitors.
The committed base64 APP_KEY is used whenever the env var is absent, letting anyone with the repository forge and decrypt session cookies and any Crypt:: payload.
allowed_origins is '*' while supports_credentials is true on line 38, so any site a signed-in customer visits can read authenticated API responses from the portal.
The session cookie is readable from document.cookie, so a single script injection anywhere in the portal yields a full session takeover.
With secure false and same_site 'none', the browser will attach the session cookie to a plain http request, so a network attacker only needs to provoke one http navigation to capture it.
The ?q= value is interpolated directly into the LIKE clause of a DB::select while the sibling account_id is bound, so a quote in the query string breaks out of the literal.
show() resolves the invoice by primary key with no account_id predicate, unlike update() and download(), so any signed-in customer can read another tenant's invoice by incrementing the id.
forceFill($request->all()) bypasses the model's $fillable and $guarded lists, letting a customer set total_cents, credit_applied_cents or paid_at on their own invoice.
The production SQL Server password for fleet_app is committed in the deployed configuration file, so repository or image access is database access.
Production points at tcp:// on 1883 with TLS disabled, so gateway credentials and all device telemetry cross the network unencrypted and can be injected by anyone on the path.
Lifetime validation is switched off (and skew widened to a day) in production, so a bearer token captured once is accepted forever with no revocation path.
FromSqlRaw is handed an interpolated string, so the ?q= value is concatenated into the SQL text rather than parameterised as it would be by FromSqlInterpolated.
[AllowAnonymous] overrides the fallback policy on a destructive endpoint that also does no tenant check, so an unauthenticated DELETE retires any device in the fleet by id.
A custom SignatureValidator that just constructs a JwtSecurityToken returns the parsed token without verifying it, so any caller can mint a token with arbitrary tenant_id and role claims.
The api and migrate services embed the flags database password in the compose file even though the db service reads the same password from a docker secret.
Mounting the host docker socket into the request-serving container turns any code execution in the API into root on the host.
is_admin is true when the caller-controlled X-Flags-Elevate header says so, so any holder of an ordinary token can send one header and gain flag create, archive and force-rollout rights.
The `term` argument is inline-formatted into the ILIKE literals of the query text while tenant_id is bound, so a quote in ?q= escapes the string and rewrites the statement.
The URL is taken verbatim from the flag's webhook_url, which upsert accepts unvalidated, so setting it to a link-local or internal address makes the service POST to it from inside the VPC.

planted.class: Debug mode left on in production
planted.note: DEBUG defaults to on unless DJANGO_DEBUG is explicitly set to something other than "1", exposing Django's technical 500 page with settings, SQL and environment to anyone who triggers an error.
The committed fallback SECRET_KEY signs sessions, password-reset tokens and CSRF tokens whenever the env var is missing, so it can be used to forge an authenticated session.
Both the session and CSRF cookies are allowed onto plain http requests, so anyone on the branch-office segment can lift an agent's session from an http hop.
pickle.loads is fed a base64 cookie value the browser fully controls, so a crafted hd_filters cookie yields remote code execution in the web process.
The ?next= value is passed to redirect() with no url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme check, so a link to the sign-in page can bounce a freshly authenticated agent to an attacker's host.
`dest` is built from the ?filename= value that ticket_export forwards untouched, and lands in a shell=True command, so a filename containing a semicolon runs as the Celery worker.
The matcher excludes /api, so the middleware session gate never runs on the route handlers, and app/api/share/route.ts reads and exfiltrates any note by id without a session.
The request's Origin header is echoed back with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials true, so any origin can read authenticated workspace responses from a signed-in user's browser.

planted.class: Reliance on cookies without integrity checking
planted.note: The session cookie is plain base64 JSON with no signature or MAC, so a user can re-encode it with another userId, another workspaceId or role 'admin' and be trusted everywhere readSession is used.
The action checks only that someone is signed in, then saves to whatever note id the form carries, never comparing existing.workspace_id or existing.owner_id against the session.

This SECURITY DEFINER function has no SET search_path (unlike archive_account below it) and references journals, entries and audit_log unqualified, so a caller with TEMP rights can shadow them from pg_temp and have the owner role write into their tables.
The file just written with the ledger_app password is chmod 0644, so every local account on the database host can read the application's database credential.

planted.class: Download of code without integrity check
planted.note: The extra migration bundle is pulled over plain http with no checksum or signature and its .sql files are then executed as ledger_owner, so anyone able to answer that hostname owns the database.

planted.class: Incorrect permission assignment for critical resource
planted.note: chmod -R 0777 on the export volume lets any local account read every tenant's statement bundle and replace one before the archiver picks it up.

decoys.ruled_out_by: app/Http/Controllers/InvoiceController.php:71 casts the query parameter with (int) before it reaches the string, so $days is an integer.

decoys.looks_like: Missing brute-force lockout on the sign-in handler
decoys.ruled_out_by: routes/web.php:22 attaches throttle:5,1 to the login.attempt route, so the framework answers 429 before the controller is entered on the sixth attempt.

decoys.looks_like: Password reset token built from md5 and mt_rand
decoys.ruled_out_by: Nothing calls legacyResetToken; routes/web.php:25 and :29 reach only sendResetLink and resetPassword, and the token those mint comes from bin2hex(random_bytes(32)) at app/Http/Controllers/AuthController.php:65.

decoys.looks_like: A committed HMAC signature value
decoys.ruled_out_by: The hex string sits inside the class docblock illustrating the processor's published header format; the secret actually used is fetched at app/Http/Middleware/VerifyWebhookSignature.php:37 from config('services.payments.webhook_secret').

decoys.looks_like: Command injection via an unescaped argument in exec()
decoys.ruled_out_by: app/Services/PdfRenderer.php:33 builds $target with sprintf('%s/invoice-%d.pdf', ...) whose %d coerces the id to an integer, and the id is cast to int by app/Models/Invoice.php:37.

decoys.looks_like: Wildcard CORS policy on the API
decoys.ruled_out_by: The policy is never made the default; Program.cs:64 and :68 attach it only to /healthz and /version, and Program.cs:70 gives the controllers the origin-restricted "console" policy instead.

decoys.looks_like: Path traversal through a route segment used in Path.Combine
decoys.ruled_out_by: The parameter is typed FirmwareChannel, the four-value enum at Models/FleetModels.cs:9, so model binding rejects the request before the action runs unless the segment names one of them.

decoys.looks_like: A committed JWT signing key
decoys.ruled_out_by: It is the published RFC 7515 A.1 example octet sequence (noted at appsettings.json:17) and no code reads that key: Services/TokenService.cs:20 and :41 read Jwt:SigningKey, supplied from the UserSecretsId at FleetApi.csproj:8 or the environment.

decoys.looks_like: API keys compared as unsalted MD5 digests
decoys.ruled_out_by: The scheme is never registered: Program.cs:21 adds only JwtBearer, and nothing in the tree references LegacyApiKeyHandler.SchemeName.

decoys.looks_like: Endpoint with no authorization attribute
decoys.ruled_out_by: Program.cs:31 sets a FallbackPolicy of RequireAuthenticatedUser, so every action without its own attribute already demands a bearer token.

decoys.looks_like: SQL injection through an interpolated ORDER BY clause
decoys.ruled_out_by: sort and dir are the SortKey and SortDir enums from src/model.rs:7 and :33, and src/model.rs:15 and :39 map them to fixed &'static str column names.

decoys.looks_like: SQL injection through an interval literal
decoys.ruled_out_by: window_hours is i64: src/routes.rs:87 extracts it with Path<(String, i64)> so a non-numeric segment 404s, and src/routes.rs:96 clamps it to 1..=720 before the call.

decoys.looks_like: Row fetched by primary key with no tenant predicate
decoys.ruled_out_by: The only caller, src/routes.rs:76, passes an id that came from src/routes.rs:71 flag_id_for_key(pool, who.tenant_id, key), which is already scoped to the caller's tenant.

decoys.looks_like: CORS layer allowing any origin
decoys.ruled_out_by: src/main.rs:116 attaches probe_cors only to the two-route probes Router, while src/main.rs:119 gives the /api/v1 tree the console layer built at src/main.rs:101 from the configured origin list.

decoys.looks_like: A committed bearer token
decoys.ruled_out_by: It is the published RFC 7519 section 3.1 example token (src/auth.rs:67) inside the #[cfg(test)] module at src/auth.rs:63, used only to assert that the Bearer prefix is stripped.

decoys.looks_like: Webhook signature computed with MD5

decoys.looks_like: OS command injection through a filename in a shell=True command
decoys.ruled_out_by: stored_path is built at tickets/models.py:84 from the row's uuid hex plus the extension, and that extension can only be one of the literals in tickets/forms.py:8 because tickets/forms.py:28 rejects anything else.

decoys.looks_like: SQL injection in a raw() query
decoys.ruled_out_by: tickets/views.py:74 wraps the query parameter in int() before it reaches the statement, so queue_id is an integer.

decoys.looks_like: View missing the @login_required decorator its siblings carry

decoys.looks_like: Delete permission granted to every staff user
decoys.ruled_out_by: tickets/admin.py:16 get_queryset filters non-superusers to their own organization, and the admin change, delete and history views resolve the object through that queryset.

decoys.looks_like: SQL injection through an interpolated LIMIT

decoys.looks_like: Session integrity check based on an unkeyed MD5 digest
